articles.title: Next.js 16.3 Released
articles.description: The newly expanded Next.js team (now including Dan Abramov and 𝕏 Pete Hunt!) has dropped the latest version of the popular React framework, complete with faster builds, optional TypeScript 7 type checking, faster SSR, Instant Navigations, AI improvements, and more.
articles.author: The Next.js Team

articles.title: Let's Make the Worst htmx Ever
articles.description: After making the 'worst' React and Vue.js implementations, Serge tackles rebuilding the essence of htmx from scratch. A fun way to understand what htmx actually does under the hood.
articles.author: Serge Zaitsev

articles.title: The Secure Way to Release an npm Package in 2026
articles.description: A practical guide to publishing npm packages more safely, written by the author of numerous popular packages (e.g. postcss). As well as showing how to use staged publishing and trusted publishing, he explains why they help.
articles.author: Andrey Sitnik

articles.title: Your SPA is Leaking Memory: 'Soak Test' It
articles.description: How to run a Playwright 'soak test' that loops a user flow within the same browser context, watches DOM node and listener counts, and fails CI when a memory leak creeps in.
articles.author: Den Odell

articles.title: Your JSON is Lying to You
articles.description: A reminder that a JSON.parse/JSON.stringify round-trip is far from lossless, with big integers, undefined, Date, and more, altered or lost along the way. Gabor covers the nastier gotchas and practical ways to make the conversion boundaries explicit.
articles.author: Gabor Koos

articles.title: cdnjs at 9 Billion Requests a Day: A Migration Story
articles.description: cdnjs is a popular, free CDN for loading JavaScript libraries without bundling or self-hosting (which LLMs really seem to like). Cloudflare explains how it now runs entirely on Workers and R2.
articles.author: Simona Badoiu (Cloudflare)

articles.title: Adding Go's defer to the TypeScript Compiler
articles.description: In Go, defer delays the execution of a function call until the surrounding function finishes. Can you just fork TypeScript and add language features? Yes! Should you? Probably not, as using is already a good fit for the use case.
articles.author: Andrew Healey

articles.title: TanStack Charts: A New Chart Grammar Option
articles.description: In the past few weeks, TanStack has been rapidly iterating on a new, framework-neutral way to declaratively specify a large number of chart-related visualizations in JavaScript. Output renders to SVG or canvas and can be styled as you wish. Here's a comparison against other established options.
articles.author: TanStack

articles.title: MicroDiff 1.6: Fast Object and Array Comparison Library
articles.description: Given two objects or arrays, it returns the differences (think diff but for JS objects). This week's release adds support for Temporal types.
articles.author: Jacob Jackson

articles.title: Virtua: Virtual List and Grid Component for Multiple Frameworks
articles.description: A fast and small virtual list/grid component for React, Vue, Solid, Svelte, and Angular. Here's a demo and a comparison table against other solutions.
articles.author: inokawa

articles.title: 📊 Perspective 5: Interactive Analytics and Data Vis Component
articles.description: Originally built by JP Morgan, a WASM-powered data visualization component suited to large and/or real-time streaming datasets. 5.0/5.1 just dropped with numerous fixes, wasm64 builds, and window columns.
articles.author: OpenJS Foundation

articles.description: 🚨 Developing incident: The popular keyv and cacheable packages were compromised today with a credential-stealing worm. The repercussions are ongoing with hundreds more packages compromised so far.
Monthly updates from the Astro team and the Svelte team. The first preview releases of SvelteKit 3 are now available.
⚖️ The Deno vs Oracle JavaScript™ trademark case rattles on with Deno consenting to a fifth extension request as discovery continues.
Popular JS library factory TanStack has rebranded and introduced new 'Markdown' and 'Highlight' libraries.
MobX 7.0 – The popular state manager slims down, removes deprecations, updates its React bindings, and now always uses Proxy-backed observable objects and arrays.
Javy 9.1 – Toolchain for compiling JavaScript to WebAssembly for WASM runtimes.
Node.js v26.6.0 (Current) and v24.19.0 (LTS)
Vite 8.2, React Three Fiber 9.7, Lerna 10.0, Hono 4.13.0

articles.title: ⚓️ Results from the 2026 State of CSS Survey
articles.description: Developers report anchor positioning as their favorite new CSS feature of this past year, though limited support is holding it back. As for the most-used newer features? :has(), aspect-ratio, and CSS nesting came out top. The results also touch on AI uptake (or lack thereof), framework adoption, the CSS grid learning curve, and more. Worth a read to get a good sense of the lay of the land.
articles.author: Sacha Greif (Devographics)

articles.title: Styling the Navigation: Declarative Route and Navigation Matching in CSS
articles.description: A look at a new CSS spec proposal from Bramus and the Chrome team. The idea is new at-rules and pseudo-classes to style View Transitions based on where you're coming from/going to, without JavaScript. It's being presented at the CSS WG meeting this week.
articles.author: Bramus Van Damme

articles.title: Gap Decorations Are Now Available, Here's What's New
articles.description: Chrome and Edge 149 are first to ship CSS gap decorations letting you style the space between grid and flex items without pseudo-element hacks. Sam, from the Edge team that drove the feature, shows off the new rule shorthand and friends.
articles.author: Sam Davis Omekarajr

articles.title: Something Nobody Told You About The Image Element: It Can Overflow!
articles.description: The <img> element has overflow: clip applied by default (not something most of us will have noticed, I'd imagine). Temani digs into why, and what happens when you make that hidden overflow visible.
articles.author: Temani Afif

articles.title: The CSS lh unit
articles.description: An accessible look at the line height unit, how it works and some use cases you may want to consider.
articles.author: Ahmad Shadeed

articles.title: Five Best Practices for Preventing Chaos in Tailwind CSS
articles.description: Originally published in 2023 and refreshed for 2026, it now includes a tailwind-best-practices skill you can give to an agent, if you like.
articles.author: Nina Torgunakova

articles.title: We Finally Learned to Center a Div, Then Browsers Added Sidebars
articles.description: When a sidebar can change what the 'center' is, do we need to target the middle of a browser window rather than the webview?
articles.author: seg6

articles.title: Web Security is Too Hard
articles.description: After trying a new Cloudflare product, Eric encountered several issues that gave him pause and distilled them into practical security advice.
articles.author: Eric Lawrence

articles.title: TIME Is Serving AI Bots a Different Website, With Ads Built In
articles.description: TIME is, amongst other things, letting ChatGPT's search index bot in to view Markdown, but blocking the training agents altogether.
articles.author: Vincent Schmalbach

articles.title: Blossom Carousel: A Native-First Carousel with Drag Support for Pointer Devices
articles.description: Most carousels replace native scrolling; Blossom builds on top of it, so you keep a real scroll container's performance and accessibility, and the drag engine is only downloaded when a mouse or trackpad is detected. Try the examples.
articles.author: Jesper Vos

articles.title: 📊 TanStack Charts: A New Way to Notate and Render Charts
articles.description: A rapidly evolving, pre-alpha, framework-agnostic way to declaratively specify a large number of chart-related visualizations in JavaScript which can then be rendered to SVG or on a canvas and styled as you wish.
articles.author: TanStack

articles.title: CSS Type Studio: A Web Tool for Fiddling with Advanced Typography with CSS
articles.description: An easy-to-use tool for visually trying out all sorts of typography features, including text wrapping, kerning, OpenType features, and more.
articles.author: CSS Type Studio

articles.title: Extend UI: An Open Source UI Kit for Modern Document Apps
articles.description: Includes 15+ components for agents, user-facing document functionality, and internal tools. Think features like a PDF viewer, DOCX editor, PowerPoint viewer, E-Signature component, and so on. Source code.
articles.author: Extend

articles.title: ffmpeg webCLI: A Browser-Based Video Editor Powered By ffmpeg.wasm
articles.description: A nicely built UI that you can try out here. Supports multiple video file types and allows you to use 30+ video operations (trim, convert, compress, flip, etc.) – all processed locally with no server upload.
articles.author: Tejaswi Gowda
